pages.text: Nobel Peace Prize AR | الأمم المتحدة Skip to main content الأمم المتحدة وجائزة نوبل للسلام الأمم المتحدة وجائزة نوبل للسلام استلهم ألفريد نوبل وصيته التي حررها عام 1895 من إيمانه بوحدة الأسرة الإنسانية. ونصّت الوصية على أن تُمنح جائزة نوبل للسلام للشخص الذي يبذل أكبر جهد في سبيل «تعزيز الأخوّة بين الأمم، وإلغاء الجيوش الدائمة أو تقليصها، وعقد مؤتمرات السلام وتشجيعها». مُنحت جائزة نوبل للسلام المرموقة 13 مرة للأمم المتحدة و وكالاتها المتخصصة وصناديقها وبرامجها ، والمنظمات المرتبطة بها، ولمسؤولين حاليين وسابقين في المنظمة. وقد نالت المفوضية السامية للأمم المتحدة لشؤون اللاجئين هذه الجائزة مرتين، في عامي 1954 و 1981 . وكرّمت لجنة نوبل النرويجية أيضًا أمينين عامين للأمم المتحدة، هما كوفي عنان و داغ همرشولد ، تقديرًا لجهودهما. وعقب فوزه بالجائزة مناصفة مع الأمم المتحدة عام 2001، أعرب الأمين العام كوفي عنان، في كلمة وجهها إلى موظفي المنظمة، عن أمله في أن «تدفعنا هذه الجائزة إلى المضي قدمًا، وتشجعنا جميعًا على النهوض بمهامنا بعزيمة أشد». «على مدى مئة عام، سعت لجنة نوبل النرويجية إلى توطيد التعاون المنظّم بين الدول. وقد أتاحت نهاية الحرب الباردة للأمم المتحدة أخيرًا أن تنهض على نحو أكمل بالدور الذي أُنشئت من أجله. وتقف المنظمة اليوم في طليعة الجهود الرامية إلى تحقيق السلام والأمن في العالم، وفي صدارة التعبئة الدولية لمواجهة التحديات الاقتصادية والاجتماعية والبيئية التي تواجه العالم... وتود لجنة نوبل النرويجية، في عامها المئوي، أن تعلن أن الطريق الوحيد القائم على التفاوض لتحقيق السلام والتعاون على الصعيد العالمي يمر عبر الأمم المتحدة». معهد نوبل النرويجي أوسلو، 12 تشرين الأول/أكتوبر 2001 الحائزون على جائزة نوبل من الأمم المتحدة 2026 - نافانيثيم بيلاي مُنحت جائزة نوبل للسلام لعام 202

After arriving she was told she had exceeded her 90-day visa-free allowance to the Schengen area and was put on a return flight, but Pugh said this was a database error and that she had only spent 22 days in the area. The European Commission said it is the responsibility of individual countries to correct any errors. The 61-year-old said the experience made her feel "like a criminal", but so far she has been unable to identify the source of the error. Her experience also cost her hundreds of pounds after she had to pay for her return flight back to the UK and she lost money she had already spent on the holiday. Pugh and her husband arrived at Reggio Calabria Airport at 12:40 BST but was denied entry. The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library is set to open in July 2026 outside Medora, North Dakota. Photograph by Image Professionals GmbH, Alamy Stock Photo By Stephanie Pearson Published October 21, 2025 Theodore Roosevelt first traveled to the Badlands on a hunting trip in 1883. He was so taken by the otherworldly landscape of pastel buttes, trilling meadowlarks, and disappearing bison, that he returned in 1884 to grieve the simultaneous deaths of his wife and mother, raising cattle and working on the wild frontier for almost three years. Its “desolate, grim beauty” so changed Roosevelt that he famously wrote, “I would not have been president had it not been for my experience in North Dakota .” Opening on July 4, 2026, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library celebrates the Badlands as much as it does the 26th president. Designed by Norwegian architectural firm Snøhetta, the state-of-the-art, sustainable library sits high on a lonely butte outside of Medora, a military camp turned frontier town named after a French nobleman’s wife. The 93,000-square-foot library disappears into its surroundings, camouflaged by a living roof sprouting native plants, part of a 1.3-mile walking trail that provides sweeping views toward the national park. The Redding-based district office oversees field offices in Alturas, Arcata, Redding and Susanville and a field station in Cedarville. The district contains two distinct regions. On the east, the Applegate and Eagle Lake field offices oversee vast expanses of public lands in a high desert landscape, including about a million and a half acres in far western Nevada. Small communities depend on public lands for economic benefits, primarily through livestock grazing, and tourism uses ranging from hunting to mountain biking. These lands provide habitat for 14 wild horse herds and special status species, such as greater sage grouse. On the west, the Arcata and Redding field offices manage smaller, scattered blocks of public land with more emphasis on recreation demands from urban areas. pages.description: An easy way for Armed Forces personnel or their families to let IRS know they're in a combat zone.
pages.text: Notifying the IRS by Email about Combat Zone Service | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Notifying the IRS by Email about Combat Zone Service More In News Working Families Tax Cuts News releases Tax relief in disaster situations Topics in the news Fact sheets IRS statements and announcements IRS Tax Tips IRS guidance Media center Tax articles to share Posters to share Working with the Department of Defense, the Internal Revenue Service identifies taxpayers who are serving in a combat zone to suspend compliance actions, such as audits or enforced collections, until 180 days after the taxpayer has left the zone. Taxpayers, including civilian taxpayers working with U.S. Armed Forces, qualifying for such combat zone relief may also notify the IRS directly of their status through combatzone@irs.gov . They should provide their name, stateside address, date of birth, and the date of deployment to the combat zone. Taxpayers should also include any official document that indicates their area or military operation. Civilians usually provide a Letter of Authorization or a letter from their employer. However, letters from the military that state the taxpayer served in a tax-free zone or Combat Zone Tax Exclusion (CZTE) area are acceptable. Do not include any Social Security numbers in an email. The taxpayer, taxpayer's spouse, or an authorized agent or representative may make this notification. The IRS cannot provide tax account information by email. pages.text: NRW taken to court over claims of risk to River Wye and Severn Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Campaigners take claim 'regulatory gap' risks poultry farms polluting rivers to High Court 17 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Steffan Messenger Wales environment correspondent BBC The legal action against Natural Resources Wales landed in the High Court River campaigners are taking on Wales' environmental regulator in the High Court over what they believe is a "regulatory gap" that risks pollution from poultry farms in two rivers. River Action UK has accused Natural Resources Wales (NRW) of not doing enough to assess or address any risk to local rivers and and other water bodies when plans for three farms in Powys were approved last year. It follows years of debate over the alleged impact of chicken farming on rivers such as the Wye and Severn - in an area dubbed the UK's "poultry capital" . NRW said it would be inappropriate to comment ahead of the court case, but that it would "participate fully in the legal process". The case is about plans to increase the capacity of three Powys farms by a combined 336,900 chickens, bringing the total to 522,000. The three farms are Neuadd Isaf, Rhosddu and Llanshay. Two of the farms, Rhosddu and Llanshay, are in the River Severn catchment while Neuadd Isaf is in the River Wye catchment. On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips. For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets. With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years. Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns. But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere. pages.text: O*NET | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content O*NET More in This Section Close O*NET Career Exploration Tools O*NET Contacts O*NET Data Collection Program O*NET Additional Information The O*NET system is maintained by a regularly updated database of occupational characteristics and worker requirements information across the U.S. economy. It describes occupations in terms of the knowledge, skills, and abilities required as well as how the work is performed in terms of tasks, work activities, and other descriptors. O*NET database Content Model Every occupation requires a different mix of knowledge, skills, and abilities, and is performed using a variety of activities and tasks. These distinguishing characteristics, or "descriptors", of an occupation are collected, codified, and described by the O*NET Content Model . This hierarchical model starts with six domains (or categories), describing the day-to-day aspects of the job and the qualifications and interests of the typical worker. The model includes nearly 277 descriptors collected by the O*NET program, along with other occupational data collected by other federal agencies such as the Bureau of Labor Statistics . Data Collection Real-world information The Data Collection program brings the Content Model frameworks to life with results from the working public. The O*NET database is collected and updated through ongoing surveys of workers in each occupation supplemented in some cases by occupation experts. OAK RIDGE, Tenn. — Oak Ridge Office of Environmental Management (OREM) crews are set to remediate soil across a portion of a 100-acre footprint for a Cold War scrapyard, representing another critical step toward reducing environmental risk and returning valuable land to productive use. The White Wing Scrap Yard served as a disposal area for contaminated equipment and debris generated during legacy operations across the Oak Ridge Reservation. OREM cleanup contractor United Cleanup Oak Ridge (UCOR) cleared 39 acres of trees and packaged over 500 bags of legacy soil after excavating more than 3 acres of land in the footprint’s north boundary. This article is more than 7 months old Despite Trump’s claims, California city has found success in lowering deadly violence, thanks to pioneering efforts to steer people down a different path Supported by About this content Abené Clayton in Oakland Mon 16 Mar 2026 10.00 EDT Last modified on Mon 16 Mar 2026 12.56 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google I n the summer of 2025, as Donald Trump rolled out his plan to deploy the national guard to Washington DC and Chicago, he suggested other American cities were overrun with violence and could soon see federal troops: Memphis, Los Angeles, New York. Oakland, the president argued , was beyond saving. “And then you have, of course, Baltimore and Oakland. They’re so far gone. We don’t even talk about that any more,” Trump said. But as Trump was making these comments, Oakland was in the midst of a historic drop in homicides. The Bay Area city ended 2025 with 67 people killed, according to data from the Oakland police department, half of its 2021 high of 134. It’s the lowest number of violent deaths recorded in 25 years. Photograph: Richard Ellis/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock Climate crisis This article is more than 4 months old Ocean surface temperatures hit a record high for June This article is more than 4 months old European scientists warn of consequences for weather patterns, the global climate and marine life Jonathan Watts Wed 1 Jul 2026 03.00 BST Last modified on Wed 1 Jul 2026 03.02 BST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Temperatures on the ocean surface have hit a record high, raising fears of another burst of extreme heat this summer. On 21 June, temperatures outside the polar regions exceeded the extraordinary highs observed at the same time in 2023 and 2024, the Copernicus Climate Change Service said on Wednesday. It warned the new peak would probably bring “consequences for weather patterns, global climate and marine ecosystems”, not least because it would coincide with the earliest phases of an El Niño event they forecast to be the strongest in decades. When the previous ocean record for June was set in 2023, scientists described the trends as “worrying”, “terrifying” and “bonkers” because they were so far outside their expectations. Office of the General Counsel The Office of the General Counsel is responsible for providing comprehensive legal services to the Secretary, Deputy Secretary, and all Departmental elements, except the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, and for effectively representing the Department as counsel before Federal, State, and other governmental agencies and courts. These services are intended to advance the missions and objectives of the Department through advice, negotiation, rulemaking, legislation, regulatory enforcement and, when necessary, litigation, and to ensure that the Department operates in compliance with all pertinent laws and regulations. Office of General Counsel Organization Chart The General Counsel is charged by the Secretary of Energy with the authority to determine the Department’s authoritative position on any question of law. The Office of the General Counsel provides legal advice, counsel, and support to the Secretary, the Deputy Secretary, and program offices throughout DOE to further the Department’s mission of advancing the national, economic, and energy security of the United States through scientific and technological innovation and the environmental cleanup of the national nuclear weapons complex. About our office Small businesses in high-unemployment, low-income areas can receive an economic boost from the HUBZone contracting program. pages.text: Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral La Oficina de Normas de Gestión Laboral (Office of Labor-Management Standards, u OLMS, por sus siglas en inglés) pertenece al Departamento de Trabajo de los Estados Unidos y es responsable de administrar y aplicar la mayoría de las disposiciones de la Ley de Notificación y Divulgación Gestión Laboral (Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act, o LMRDA, por sus siglas en inglés). Dicha ley fue adoptada con el fin de garantizar normas básicas de democracia y responsabilidad fiscal en las organizaciones laborales del sector privado. Los sindicatos que representan a los empleados del Correo Postal de los Estados Unidos también se hallan sujetos a la LMRDA. Los sindicatos de empleados federales se hallan sujetos a normas similares conforme a la Ley de Reforma del Servicio Civil de 1978 (Civil Service Reform Act, o CSRA, por sus siglas in inglés) y a la Ley del Servicio Exterior de 1980. La OLMS anima a que los oficiales y los miembros del sindicato, así como otros individuos afectados por la LMRDA, se pongan en contacto con la agencia para discutir de problemas, presenten quejas u obtengan información sobre la LMRDA. Además, la OLMS fomenta la conformidad voluntaria con la LMRDA al informar a oficiales del sindicato y a otros individuos de sus responsabilidades y al animar a los miembros del sindicato a que ejerzan sus derechos. Photograph: YouTube Tetris This article is more than 2 years old Oklahoma 13-year-old believed to be first person ever to beat Tetris This article is more than 2 years old Previously only bots and AI had got game to its ‘kill screen’ but Willis Gibson managed to get game to freeze with score 999999 Blake Montgomery Wed 3 Jan 2024 13.35 EST Last modified on Mon 29 Jan 2024 05.35 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A 13-year-old in Oklahoma is believed to be the first person ever to beat Tetris since the game’s release more than three decades ago. Previously, only bots powered by artificial intelligence had forced the game, popularised by the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES) and Game Boy consoles, to the end of its “kill screen”, where its signature blocks are falling so fast that the game itself can’t continue. In a video documenting his feat and posted on Tuesday, the Oklahoma teenager, known as Blue Scuti online and by his legal name, Willis Gibson, plays for roughly 38 minutes and reaches level 157 before saying, “Oh, I missed it,” believing that a misplaced block scuttled his attempt. The Field Office administers the extraction, use, and sale of Federal minerals (primarily oil, gas, and coal). The Field Office also provides oversight to Indian mineral owners by ensuring oil and gas operations on Indian lands are conducted according to lease terms and conditions, approved plans, and existing laws and regulations. The Field Office also administers an active Wild Horse and Burro Program that accounts for 20 percent of the annual adoption target for the entire Bureau. The Wild Horse and Burro staff conducts 12-15 satellite adoptions per year in locations throughout BLM New Mexico’s four-state jurisdiction resulting in the adoption of nearly 600 animals annually.
